clue.text: Rewrite badly bewilders character most often seen in Hollywood

indicators.note: letters treated badly are knocked out of shape, so this word signals a rearrangement

parts.words: character most often seen in Hollywood
parts.note: the letter O appears three times in Hollywood, more than any other

explanation.surface: A complaint that some clumsy rewriting baffles one of the stars you see most often in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges BEWILDERS plus O. The definition is just 'Rewrite', in the sense of censoring a text the way Thomas Bowdler cleaned up Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Expurgating a text by cutting the improper bits is a particular kind of rewriting, named after the editor Thomas Bowdler.

clue.text: Cable of a ship, perhaps, was twisted internally

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the pronoun, within it

parts.note: ships are traditionally referred to as she or her

indicators.note: the word was is twisted out of its usual order

explanation.surface: A description of a ship's rope that was twisted inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships are traditionally female in English, so 'a ship, perhaps' is a pronoun; the 'perhaps' admits not every 'her' is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used to moor or tow a vessel.

clue.text: A cry rising around rear of tenement — from this?

definitions.text: A cry rising around rear of tenement — from this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cry is a yell
CA is short for circa, Latin for around

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A wail goes up somewhere behind the tenements, and the clue asks what animal made it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns YELL into LLEY. The whole clue also defines: a yowl from behind a tenement building is just what a stray cat would make.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray city cat living in back lanes is known for yowling at night behind buildings.

clue.text: Brought before court around end of October, being forced to beg?

indicators.note: the phrase for appearing in court goes around the letter

parts.note: to be had up is to be summoned before a court

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone hauled into court near Halloween, apparently because poverty drove them to begging.
explanation.walkthrough: HAD UP goes 'around' R, the last letter of October, giving HAR D UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone short of money may be driven to begging, which the question mark marks as an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Go with staff to cover hospital observation point

parts.note: go is a euphemism for urinate, to pee

indicators.note: the staff covers the hospital letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a staff is a pole
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Instructions to head off with colleagues to cover a hospital's observation post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' and 'staff' read as setting off with employees, but they mean PEE and POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hole through which one can look is literally a point from which to observe.

clue.text: Go in peace, no end of peace

indicators.note: no signals that something is removed from the word for peace

parts.note: peace and quiet go together; quiet means peace

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A farewell blessing, 'go in peace', apparently with endless peace.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIET loses E, the last letter of 'peace', which 'no' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a job or place is to depart, the simple sense of going.

clue.text: Star appearing late in year, near start of Advent

parts.note: November, abbreviated Nov, comes late in the year

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A star shows up in the sky in late November, close to the beginning of Advent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares to great brightness and then fades.

clue.text: Left queasy (not at first) after swallowing one of flowering plants

indicators.note: the trimmed word takes the other piece inside it
the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: feeling bilious is feeling sick
an ace is a one on playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone left feeling sick after swallowing a flower, perhaps a poisonous lily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only says the rest follows L. The definition is an adjective phrase: the answer means belonging to the lily family.
explanation.definitionFit: Liliaceous describes the lily family, a group of flowering plants.

clue.text: Tube station rebuilt for a central stage?

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new shape, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A London Underground station refurbished to give it a central stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster Gate is a London Underground (Tube) stop on the Central line, so 'central' quietly hints at it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster Gate is one of the named stations on the London Underground's Central line.

clue.text: Like a long journey, taking days, eons, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An epic trip described as lasting days, even eons.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's hero Odysseus spent ten years wandering home, so the adjective describes an epic voyage.

clue.text: American law officer you had once taken aback about post

indicators.note: the reversed letters go about the other piece
taken aback means turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: ye'd is an old way of saying you had
to post a notice is to put it up

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned sentence: a US sheriff's helper was startled by something you once posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reverses YE'D (archaic 'you had') to DEY, which goes 'about' PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a sheriff's assistant who enforces the law is called by this title.

clue.text: While lacking heart, moving fast as regards rhythm

indicators.note: the two central letters of the eight-letter word go missing

parts.note: a meteoric rise moves at great speed, like a meteor

explanation.surface: A dancer or song losing its emotional core while rushing along, judged on rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking heart' removes EO, the middle two of METEORIC's eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrical or metric verse is organised by its beats, so the adjective concerns rhythm.

clue.text: Regard program: competitor has nothing for one

parts.note: an app is a software program

indicators.note: for signals that one item stands in place of another

parts.note: a rival is a competitor
I is the Roman numeral for one
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rival software maker's verdict on a program, where nothing replaced the top entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regard' is the noun, as in holding someone in high esteem, not the verb 'look at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding someone in high regard means showing favour or esteem toward them.

clue.text: A gossip accepting guy is something quite unreal

indicators.note: the word for gossip accepts the name inside itself

parts.note: to natter is to chat or gossip
Tim stands for any guy, a man's name

explanation.surface: A chatterbox who takes in some fellow, and the result is pure fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' stands for any man's name, here a short one; 'gossip' is a verb meaning chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter made of antiparticles sounds like science fiction, the stuff of fantastical physics rather than everyday life.

clue.text: What indicates event from evident modern crime?

parts.note: remove the letters ID from the word evident and you are left with event, so ID has been stolen

explanation.surface: A puzzle question: which modern crime is plainly evident?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'ID entity theft': stealing ID from EVIDENT leaves EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing someone's personal details to impersonate them is a fraud of the internet age.

clue.text: Assess Greek character turning up during English Depression

indicators.note: the reversed letter sits during, inside, the valley

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Weighing up a Greek figure who appears in the middle of England's economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses TAU to UAT, set 'during' VALE. 'Depression' looks economic but is a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to weigh up or judge the worth of something.

clue.text: Hour in control of ship — an exciting event

indicators.note: the hour abbreviation goes in the steering word

parts.note: a tiller is the lever used to steer a boat

explanation.surface: An hour at the helm of a ship makes for real excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that gives a thrill, such as a gripping game or story, counts as exciting.

clue.text: Put off carrying tin — this is more like a bottle

definitions.text: this is more like a bottle

indicators.note: the word for put off carries the container inside it

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged from carrying a tin, told a bottle would suit better.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel for serving wine, shaped much like a stoppered bottle rather than a tin.

clue.text: Start missing from account written up about university performers

indicators.note: the reversed letters go about the university letter
in a down clue, written up means read upwards, backwards
the first letter is taken off

parts.note: a report is an account

explanation.surface: A newspaper write-up of university actors that lacks an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: REPORT loses its start to give EPORT; 'written up' reverses that to TROPE, which goes 'about' U.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of actors, dancers or other entertainers.

clue.text: Government, say, will block historic poem

indicators.note: the example abbreviation blocks the middle of the poem word, sitting within it

parts.note: rime is an old spelling of rhyme, as in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner
e.g. means for example, as say does

explanation.surface: Someone warns that the government will ban a classic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'historic' points to the old spelling of rhyme used in Coleridge's famous title.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a system or period of rule, a government.

clue.text: Gross — 3 heading off the worse for wear

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off

parts.note: the answer to 3 down is a stray cat; another word for a cat is moggy

explanation.surface: Something gross, with the third item gone, is past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points at 3 down, the alley cat; MOGGY is British slang for a mongrel cat, which loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling groggy is feeling dazed and unsteady, as if a little the worse for drink.

clue.text: Fake work securing subscriptions is rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse
the work word secures the other inside it

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
dues are subscriptions paid to a club

explanation.surface: A sham piece of work about collecting subscriptions gets turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: OP 'securing' DUES makes ODUESP; 'is rejected' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means sham or not genuine, pretending to be something it is not.

clue.text: Promoted best place

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, which in a down clue reads the word from the bottom

parts.note: the tops means the best

explanation.surface: Someone promoted to the top position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoted' reverses TOPS in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a location or place.

clue.text: Subtle tricks to import lines: very good sweets

indicators.note: the tricks word brings the other pieces inside it

parts.note: arts are cunning tricks or wiles
L is the abbreviation for line, LL for lines
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: Cunning tricks smuggle in lines of very good sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Liquorice allsorts are a British mixed bag of liquorice sweets; 'Subtle tricks' is a noun phrase, cunning arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice allsorts are a British assortment of chewy liquorice confectionery.

clue.text: Spokesperson likely to suffer a blow?

definitions.meaning: someone who speaks on behalf of others
the part of a wind instrument that the player blows into

explanation.surface: A spokesperson who seems bound to get punched.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesperson voices others' views, and a trumpet's blown part shares its name.

clue.text: Part song, part jungle EP

indicators.note: part says the letters are a piece of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Part of a song from a jungle music EP.
explanation.walkthrough: A glee is an unaccompanied part song for several voices; 'part' first reads as a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an English unaccompanied song for three or more voices in parts.
